expert_role: Software architect and licence/source gatekeeper (BIM interoperability, web geometry, open-data licensing)

findings.issue: The core fallback mesher cannot work as written for Brep polysurfaces. The spec says 'planar Brep faces are triangulated from edge loops with earcut', but rhino3dm binds no BrepLoop or BrepTrim and no face-to-edge adjacency, in JS or Python. In bnd_brep.cpp, BrepFace exposes only underlyingSurface, createExtrusion, duplicateFace, duplicateSurface, getMesh, setMesh and orientationIsReversed, and BrepEdge is a bare CurveProxy. Closed polysurfaces from BooleanUnion, Cap or Grasshopper bakes with no saved render mesh are the usual massing case after extrusions. They would all land in the 'unmeshed, blocking' line, so the FSR and height checks never run for these entrants.
findings.fix: Use a route the bindings support. For each face, call isPlanar on its underlying surface. Then call face.duplicateFace(false), which returns a single-face Brep whose edges() are only that face's boundary. Sample each edge, chain the samples into loops by endpoint within a weld tolerance, and project them with frameAt. Take the largest |signed area| as the outer loop, then run earcut and the area-deviation check. Weld vertices across faces before handing the mesh to manifold-3d (Mesh.merge). Add a CI fixture: a BooleanUnion polysurface saved with no render meshes. Until this passes, mark the metric 'ProgramVolumes without usable mesh' as unverified.

findings.issue: Speckle is listed as 'Apache-2.0' in M01, M02 and M06. The speckle-server LICENSE says code under packages/server/modules/workspaces/ and packages/server/modules/gatekeeper/ is under the Speckle Enterprise Edition licence, and only the rest is Apache-2.0. The GitHub API reports the licence as NOASSERTION. The M02 row 'Speckle connectors and file importers' also points at the speckle-server URL, so the connectors' own licence has not been checked.
findings.fix: Record the licence as 'Apache-2.0 except EE modules (workspaces, gatekeeper)'. State that a self-hosted server either excludes the EE directories or accepts the EE terms. Cite the connectors' own repository and its licence. Add these to the CI licence-column check.

findings.issue: The platform's own licence, the inbound licence for community-uploaded modules, and the licence for shared design-state data are still undecided ('team decision'), but the spec ships public module upload and forking. Without these, nobody can lawfully fork a contributed module, and LGPL, GPL, MPL and ODbL pieces cannot be checked for compatibility. The previous round asked for this ('State the licence that applies to uploaded modules and to the project itself').
findings.fix: Before any public upload, choose a platform licence compatible with MPL-2.0 web-ifc (for example Apache-2.0 or MPL-2.0). Require an SPDX id and a DCO sign-off in every module manifest, and have CI reject GPL code in the browser bundle. Default design states to 'all rights reserved by owner', with an explicit CC choice when published. Tag ODbL-derived context layers so they never enter a fork without ODbL notice and share-alike.

findings.issue: Status labels are still inconsistent, a residue of the previous round's item. Four live metrics keep 'false_assumption_corrected': true-north error, site position agreement, ProgramVolumes without usable mesh, and mapping coverage. Their thresholds are team presets. The TEAM_ASSUMPTION flag says r2 reset corrected metrics 'so the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour marks only the logged claims', which contradicts these four labels. One of the four now rests on the infeasible edge-loop route.
findings.fix: Set the four to team_assumption, or to verified where a threshold is sourced, and link each one to its FALSE_ASSUMPTION log entry. Reserve the special colour for log entries only.

findings.issue: The UNVERIFIED flag on the IFC4 ADD2 attributes can be closed from a source the spec already cites (web-ifc ifc-schema.ts, P14-S07). Its IFC4 namespace has IfcBuildingStorey(..., CompositionType, Elevation), IfcBuilding(..., ElevationOfRefHeight, ElevationOfTerrain), IfcSite(..., RefElevation), IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion(..., Scale) with no IfcMapConversionScaled, IfcProjectedCRS.VerticalDatum, and IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure with RelatingStructure typed IfcSpatialElement. IFC4 also has IfcExternalSpatialElement, the class intended for exterior space, yet OpenSpace maps to an 'external IfcSpace'.
findings.fix: Move the attribute existence to resolved, citing web-ifc's IFC4 schema, and keep only behaviour for the round-trip spike. Map OpenSpace to IfcExternalSpatialElement under IfcSite (PredefinedType EXTERNAL), with external IfcSpace as a fallback.

findings.issue: The 'Agreement with organiser reference heights' check compares maxht_m with CTBUH heights, but maxht_m is not a part height. API query for bldgid 149845: the tallest part has hgt_agl 192.95 m (top 223.71, base 30.76), while maxht_m is 208.63, which implies a base about 15.1 m geodetic, well below the 30.7 m tower base. The 208.6 versus 201 m '3.8% agreement' mixes conventions.
findings.fix: Compute context heights as part topelev_m minus the ground or entrance elevation at the tower, which matches the CTBUH convention used elsewhere. Use maxht_m only as a flagged summary, and restate the r2 indicative check.

findings.issue: Public forks unlock after 30 Nov, but terms 5.3 say the jury learns identities only after winners are selected, and results are due 26 Jan 2027. A named public fork in December or January can de-anonymise an entry. Separately, the organiser's resubmit page says previously published concepts may be reused if 'all presentation materials must be visually updated'. That narrows the 4.1 conflict to visual materials. The deadline is also 23:59 London (15:59 Vancouver).
findings.fix: Extend the default warning or block to 26 Jan 2027, with an owner override and a warning. Store deadlines in UTC. Add the resubmit page as a source and narrow the unresolved 4.1 question to rendered views and boards.

findings.issue: Core modules M03 and M05 list the v1 module M08 in depends_on. The CI rule that 'each depends_on equals the producers of its inputs' then makes core builds depend on a v1 module.
findings.fix: Split depends_on into required and optional_inputs, and have CI check acyclicity over both but core completeness only over required.

findings.issue: The FSR wording is wrong: '1% of the denominator is about 1,032 m2'. 1% of 11,468 m2 is about 115 m2. The intended claim is that a 1% change in the denominator moves the required employment area by about 1,032 m2.
findings.fix: Reword it that way, and show both numbers on the area table.

findings.issue: The local IfcClassification for the 9 tags has no Name, Edition, EditionDate or Source, so IFC tools cannot tell which vocabulary version a tag comes from after a schema change.
findings.fix: Declare IfcClassification 'VTC Layer0 tags', with Edition equal to schema_version, an EditionDate, and Source set to the repository URL of the vocabulary file. Add these to the round-trip diff.

findings.issue: The vertical datum is recorded as 'CGVD28GVRD or CGVD2013', but no conversion between them is specified. LiDAR is CGVD28GVRD, and view-limit and footprint datums are unknown, so a mixed-datum Z0 can hide inside the 1 m / 3 m Z0 thresholds.
findings.fix: Add a vertical-datum conversion parameter (geoid or height-transformation model, with source) and refuse to compare elevations across datums without it. Record the conversion in provenance.

findings.issue: The hosted-API data-handling description is incomplete. Anthropic's structured-outputs page marks ZDR as eligible but 'Excludes Covered Models', and caches the JSON schema for up to 24 hours. The privacy page confirms 30-day default deletion.
findings.fix: Record the model id, its ZDR eligibility and the schema caching in the opt-in dialog and in P14-M06 provenance. Keep the rules-only mode as the default.

findings.issue: opencascade.js is effectively unmaintained. The GitHub API shows pushed_at 2023-08-15, about three years ago, and no releases are listed. The spec only says 'maintenance unclear'.
findings.fix: State it as stale and keep it in the roadmap only. Evaluate maintained alternatives for STEP/B-rep reading (for example occt-import-js, which Online 3D Viewer uses) before committing, and record their licences.

findings.issue: The City Open Government Licence text is still unread: the portal licence page is script-rendered and returned no text. The attribution-completeness metric therefore cites terms nobody has seen. ODbL layers are said to be 'separable', but the snapshot manifest hashes a single context_layer_hash that forks copy.
findings.fix: Have a person read the licence and record its attribution string. Hash City and ODbL layers separately in the manifest, and attach the ODbL notice to any fork that carries the ODbL hash.

findings.issue: proj4js is still marked 'MIT per project (LICENSE.md not read)'. The LICENSE.md is MIT-style (copyright 2014, Adair et al.). The datum code also confirms the r2 correction: datum.js multiplies params 3-5 by SEC_TO_RAD, and datumUtils uses position-vector formulas.
findings.fix: Mark the licence as verified, and cite the two code lines as evidence for the arc-second position-vector parameters.

false_assumptions.claim: The rhino3dm fallback mesher can triangulate planar Brep faces 'from edge loops with earcut'
false_assumptions.why_false: rhino3dm (JS and Python) exposes no BrepLoop or BrepTrim and no face-to-edge mapping. BrepFace binds only underlyingSurface, createExtrusion, duplicateFace, duplicateSurface, getMesh, setMesh and orientationIsReversed, and BrepEdge is a bare CurveProxy.
false_assumptions.correction: Rebuild each face's loops from face.duplicateFace(false).edges() by chaining endpoints, use the surface's isPlanar and frameAt, then run earcut and weld vertices across faces. Test on a BooleanUnion fixture with no render meshes.
false_assumptions.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcneel/rhino3dm/main/src/bindings/bnd_brep.cpp (lines 392-412 Python and 463-522 JS: no loop or trim classes); bnd_surface.cpp binds isPlanar, frameAt and normalAt

verdict: Gate fails. Round 3 fixed most of the previous round's items: north types, the EPSG:3157 parameters (I confirmed them against the proj4js code), the acyclic graph, has_floor, schema_version and the schedule. Several problems remain. The core fallback mesher assumes Brep edge loops that rhino3dm does not bind, so typical Boolean polysurfaces would stay blocked. Speckle is not plain Apache-2.0: its workspaces and gatekeeper modules carry an Enterprise licence. The platform, module and design-state licences are still undecided. The brief and organiser package are still unread, and the Q&A close may be 1 Nov, not 3 Nov. Four metrics keep stale status labels. The IFC4 ADD2 attribute flag can now be closed from web-ifc's schema. My web-search budget ran out mid-audit, so I used direct fetches and API queries only.
